subject: botany_2
question_text: Name the scientists who were credited for showing the role of penicillin as an antibiotic.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.49, printed question 145. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

insider_note: Three names and they must be split correctly: Fleming DISCOVERED it, Chain and Florey ESTABLISHED its role. The question asks about the second pair.

steps.why: Fleming saw the effect but could not purify enough of the substance to test it as a medicine, which is why the story does not end with him.
common_mistakes: Crediting Fleming with establishing its role as an antibiotic. He DISCOVERED it; others proved its use.
Saying he made it deliberately. The mould arrived by accident.
steps.memory_tip: Fleming saw it; he did not prove it.

steps.label: Who established its role
steps.margin_note: Both names, the shared Nobel, and the wartime use.

lines.text: Ernest Chain and Howard Florey established

lines: established the role of penicillin as an ANTIBIOTIC.
All THREE shared the Nobel Prize in 1945.
Penicillin was used extensively to treat wounded
soldiers in the Second World War.
steps.why: Turning an observation into a medicine needed purification and clinical testing, which is the work Chain and Florey did.
common_mistakes: Naming only Fleming. The question asks who showed its ROLE — that is Chain and Florey.
Naming Waksman. Waksman worked on streptomycin.
steps.memory_tip: Fleming found it; Chain and Florey made it a medicine.
